plot: Minutes before Zed's first movie night the whole street goes dark; everyone blames Rex's giant glowing sign, but Chip finds the blinking switch box — Zed plugged in too many big machines — and a grown-up, Mrs. Volt, safely switches the power back on.

script.title: Who Turned Off the Whole Street? 🔦

beats.say: Whoa! The street lights just went out! All at once!
Who turned off the whole street? Right before movie night!
My popcorn! My movie! I planned this night all week.
After the gold-cube day, the friends wanted a quiet movie night.
Zed had never hosted before. He made a list. And a snack.
Meet my new popcorn machine. Popcorn for one hundred friends!
Zed, we are only five friends. Plus Chip.
I plugged it in with the heater, fridge and disco ball.
Street brightness: zero percent. My face brightness: four percent.
Woof! Woof woof!
I know who did it. Look up there!
Across the street, one giant gold sign still glowed. It said: REX.
Isn't it beautiful? My face sign! I switched it on just now.
Five minutes ago? That's exactly when the lights went out!
No way! My sign has its own battery. I'm rich, not silly.
Then prove it, Rex. Switch it off!
Rex sighed a long sigh and switched off his beautiful sign.
Now the street was even darker. The lights did not come back.
See? Not me. And now nobody can see my face. Tragic.
The movie starts in ten minutes, and nobody can find my door!
Do not worry. I have a flashlight mode. Activating now.
Gizmo's antenna gave one tiny blink. Like a firefly with a cold.
Flashlight power: two percent. Enough to see my own nose.
New plan! Everybody walk in a line and follow my voice!
So they all walked in a line. Straight into each other.
But Chip did not walk in the line. Chip followed his nose.
Woof! Grrr. Woof woof!
Chip found something by Zed's door. A little red light!
By Zed's door, a small wall box blinked red. Click, click.
If we can't fix this, the whole street stays dark all night!
That's the switch box. It cuts power when houses use too much.
Too much power? Who would use that much power at night?
Very slowly, everyone turned to look at Zed.
Popcorn machine. Heater. Fridge. Disco ball. Oh no. It was me.
I wanted the best movie night ever. Now the street is dark.
You didn't ruin anything. You just plugged in too much at once.
Easy! I'll open the box and flip the switch back on!
Stop, Blox! Kids never open switch boxes. We call a grown-up.
I know one! I call her whenever my sign gets too shiny.
Soon Mrs. Volt arrived, with a yellow helmet and a big flashlight.
Evening, friends! Before I touch anything, unplug the big machines, please.
Unplugging the heater. Unplugging the fridge. Goodbye, disco ball.
One machine at a time is fine. Ten together? Box says no.
Mrs. Volt opened the box, pushed one switch up, and... click.
Every light on the street came back on at once!
Brightness: one hundred percent. My nose looks fantastic.
And my sign? Can my beautiful face come back too?
Only on its own battery, Rex. Deal?
Then Zed plugged in only the popcorn machine. Nothing else.
Popcorn for one hundred friends. Or six friends and Mrs. Volt!
I never say no to popcorn. Big machines, one at a time!
Best movie night ever. And the movie hasn't even started yet!
Then Chip trotted back with something in his mouth. A bus ticket!
Next time: whose ticket is it, and where does that bus go?

long.title: Who Turned Off the Whole Street? 🔦
long.description:
"I only wanted the best movie night ever… so why is the whole street dark?" — Zed
Minutes before movie night, every light on the block goes out. Everyone blames Rex's giant glowing sign, but Chip follows a tiny blinking red light… A blocky cartoon about a real-life power cut.
